title: Cello
summary: Cello notes played through a computed cello body. Limits first: A3 and the low notes are too dark, several notes are too clean, and the stopped notes sit off pitch. Every note drives a computed spruce and maple shell body with an air cavity, a finite-width hair bow, the measured rosin friction law of Woodhouse and Galluzzo (2025, eq. 13) and the printed 116 mm after-length. E2 sits 5.0 c flat of equal temperament and E3 8.1 c flat, each after one finger move and one residual-flexibility row and with its bow moved to 1/11 of its sounding length; F5's bow is at 1/11 too, which removes its line at a third of its pitch but leaves it 7 dB too clean. Eb4 is rendered at 47944 Hz to remove time-step lines, plays with the body's wood loss raised 3.25 times, near the printed damping, and has its bow at 1/11 of its sounding length too: that brings its cluster of lines near 180 Hz down to the recording's level and its attack to 342 ms, but leaves it 4 dB too clean and holding a line at 301 Hz, 39 dB under its first harmonic. D3 carries its string's measured torsion (758 Hz, 1.8 kg/s, Q 34), which moves it 1.0 c flat and off the render clock; on the body with the endpin and the printed bar its attack reads 387 ms against 381, from a shelf 3 to 6 dB under the held level to 0.35 s rather than the recording's slow rise, and its first two harmonics stay swapped. C2 now plays the s8 shell the other pages play, with the endpin and the printed bar: it scores 6 of 14 where it scored 8, and its 11th and 12th harmonics sit 25 and 28 dB further under the recording's. D3 and A3 keep 512 body modes, the others 256.
physics_present: a computed cello shell body from published plate geometry and wood data: spruce top, maple back and ribs, a 12.5 mm-class table, a 19 g bridge and 256 computed modes (D3 and A3 keep 512; D3's last mode is about 4.3 kHz)
an enclosed air cavity through a physical neck, and f-holes placed from printed caliper measurements of the Castelbarco Stradivari (Library of Congress)
the measured Kaplan string rows (Mansour 2016): tension, mass, bending stiffness and loss factors for the string played, with the bridge and bow flexibility

the exact static residual flexibility of each string's omitted bending modes (`residual-flexibility exact-static-green`): the row adds the string's omitted modes as one static compliance at the bridge and at a finger, with no fitted number; A3, C2, D3 and G2 carry it with its bow counterpart, E2 and E3 carry the support row alone (it takes the E3 note 4.5 c flat and its 180 Hz line down 11.6 dB, and the E2 note 4.8 c sharp), and Eb4 and F5 carry neither

the string's measured torsion on D3 (`torsion-measured mansour-2016-kaplan-cello-d3-open`; Mansour, Woodhouse and Scavone 2016, Part 2, section 2.2): 10 twist modes at multiples of 758 Hz, a characteristic impedance of 1.8 kg/s and Q 34 on every mode, a non-dispersive line from the nut to the bridge station with the after-length untwisted and no gas drag added. The binding of that string to this one is a reading of the two papers (Part 2 names neither the string's make nor its length; the row binds it to Part 1's Kaplan Solutions D3 at 0.69 m). On the body with the endpin and the printed bar it moves D3 1.0 c flat (146.91 Hz) and off the render clock (326.73 samples a period, steady to 1.4 c), moves H2 to H10 by 2.9 dB or less re the first and leaves 14 of 14 rows inside
a bow of finite width (a 10 mm ribbon) with hair compliance, driven by a gesture schedule of ramp, hold and lift; on D3 and A3 the bow force follows the bow speed through the start of the stroke

on E3, E2, F5 and Eb4 the bow sits 1/11 of the sounding length from the bridge, as on the open pages (25.1 mm of 276.6 mm, 50.1 mm of 551.0 mm, 20.0 mm of 220.5 mm and 44.4 mm of 487.9 mm), with the force from Schelleng's limits at that distance (the maximum goes as v/beta and the minimum as v/beta^2: Mansour, Woodhouse and Scavone 2017, eqs 3-5). The force is the geometric mean of the window, a rule chosen for these pages and stated before any render (E3 1.47 N in 0.47 to 4.60 N, E2 1.50 N in 0.49 to 4.60 N, F5 0.33 N in 0.062 to 1.78 N on the A string, Eb4 0.29 N in 0.048 to 1.78 N on the A string, where Eb4's window uses the shell table with each mode's Q rebuilt for the page's wood loss). The open pages' forces sit higher in their windows by the same arithmetic (A3's 0.7071 N and D3's 1.0 N at 0.80 and 0.78 on a log scale from the minimum to the maximum), F5's old 0.7071 N was 1.10 times Schelleng's maximum at its old distance, and Eb4's old 0.7071 N was inside its window then, at 0.85 on that scale
the measured rosin friction curve (Woodhouse and Galluzzo 2025, eq. 13) on every note
the printed 116 mm after-length, bridge to tailpiece (Fouilhe and Houssay, SMAC 2013), on every note

stopped notes: a rigid finger stop on the fingerboard (Issanchou 2017) at 1e12 N/m on the C string (E2, E3) and 1e13 N/m on the A string (F5, and Eb4 as its page), placed at the equal-tempered station and then moved once toward the named note, never toward the recording, on E2, E3 and F5; Eb4's finger is not moved
Eb4 rendered at 47944 Hz, a rate chosen so its period is a whole number of samples, and resampled to 48 kHz for the page

Eb4 plays with the body's wood loss raised 3.25 times; on free decay that takes the shell's lower strong pole from Q 67-75 with wood alone to Q 24-27, read on F5 and C2 renders with the same packs, near the 18-26 printed for a cello on a rig (Zhang and Woodhouse 2014); every other cello page keeps the wood-only loss

on A3, D3 and C2, the endpin as a point mass of 186.6 g on the shell: 0.47 m by 8 mm (Sakai and Samejima 2023, Table 3) at the 7900 kg/m3 printed there for iron, solid assumed, shared over the lower end block's 85 by 30 mm footprint from Johannsson's table, a maker's table not measured on this cello; the block's own wood is not added

on A3, D3 and C2, the bass bar at its printed place: its ends sit 83.5 and 83.4 mm from the top's ends, against 80 to 85 mm on Alan Goldblatt's cello specification sheet and 80 in a maker's forum post (Cliff Green), after sliding it 12.27 mm toward the neck from where the il Cannone mapping had put it (71.2 and 95.7 mm); its length, height, width, slant and place under the bridge's bass foot are unchanged. Goldblatt's and Johannsson's are makers' tables, borrowed and named, not measurements of this cello
physics_missing: a measured cello: the body is computed from published geometry and wood data, and no measured body admittance or string Q of this instrument is on the cards; on the C2 page the wood data are stated only from 150 Hz (maple) and 100 Hz (spruce), so that body has no mode below 150 Hz, above the C2 fundamental
body modes above the computed range: 256 modes end at 2438.5 Hz (the 512 modes of D3 and A3 at about 4.3 kHz, read for D3); the plates are resolved to about 3 kHz and the ribs not above about 1 kHz

body damping: the shell's lowest strong pole reads Q 72-78 from wood alone (free decay 67-75, receiver sweep 78), against 18 to 26 printed for a cello on a rig or foam and 13.4 held by a player (Zhang and Woodhouse 2014); the F5 page names this as a likely reason for its fault, not shown. The wood loss raised 3.25 times toward the printed damping was tried on all eight cello pages: one rose (Eb4, 10 to 11 of 14) and it darkened every page, bringing the three too-bright pages toward their recordings and the five too-dark ones away. So more wood loss isn't what the cello's top end is missing
a body-radiation skin row: the posted cards carry none

a bow that varies during the note: force and speed hold after the ramp (D3's and A3's force follows speed only through the start), so the notes repeat too exactly: harmonics-to-noise reads 43.4 dB against 30.1 in the recording on E2 and 34.9 against 30.1 on C2 (Eb4, with the printed wood loss and its bow at 1/11, reads 41.8 against 37.9, where its last page read 34.9); the Eb4 attack builds in 342 ms against 411, where its last page's was 37

time-step independence: at 48 kHz a note's period can lock to the render clock and put lines into the sound that are not in the instrument; Eb4 needed its own render rate, and F5 held a line at exactly a third of its pitch (233.0 Hz, -28.8 dB) until its bow moved to 1/11 of its sounding length, which removed it

an explanation of the finger: the bowed pitch moves 1.4 to 1.8 times the length of the move (E3 25.3 c for 17.6 c before its residual row, which takes a further 4.5 c off the note, E2 19.2 c for 10.7 c before its row, which takes a further 4.8 c up), so E2 and E3 land flat of equal temperament, and the E3 and F5 recordings sit sharp of it

the bow's omitted-mode compliance on a stopped note: the engine refuses `bow-residual-flexibility` with a finger stop (the bow/stop cross-compliance is not yet carried), so E2 and E3 have the support row only and Eb4 and F5 have neither row; F5 was tried with the support row and fell from 9 to 8 of 15 (harmonics-to-noise left its ruler, the third harmonic rose to 23.7 dB re the first, and a held line appeared at 189 Hz, -19 dB), so it stays without

the timbre balance: the low notes and A3 are too dark (centroid 238 Hz against 388 on C2, 181 against 390 on E2, 249 against 575 on E3, 353 against 868 on A3) and F5 too bright (1587 against 1187; Eb4, with the printed wood loss and its bow at 1/11, is 466 against 466); D3's first two harmonics are swapped (H2 4.6 dB over H1, the recording 7.5 dB under); on F5 the second and third harmonics now sit 3.8 and 3.6 dB over the first (the third 15.7 dB over it before), the recording 4.6 and 5.9 dB under it

the stopped notes' bow: E3 at 1/11 and the page's 0.4204 N broke to its octave (0.90 times Schelleng's minimum, rendered 11-04). With the bow at 1/11 the E3 holes at H4 and H5 did not close (-0.8 and +2.7 dB re the first), which sit in a valley of the shell's bridge mobility at 818-870 Hz; E2 now builds in level by 5.7 dB over the note, its second harmonic no longer leads its first (-2.8 dB re the first against +5.5 in the recording), and it carries a burst near the body's 190 Hz mode at 0.8-1.6 s, which no grader row measures; F5 at 1/11 with 0.33 N is clean in its motion (no octave, no subharmonic) but now reads 34.6 dB harmonics-to-noise against 27.6 in the recording, and its harmonics-to-noise, cepstral and harmonics rows left their rulers while wavelet, odd/even and attack came in (9 of 15 both ways); Eb4 at 1/11 with 0.29 N is clean in its motion (no octave, no subharmonic, one full slip per period as before, with more small slips between them: 8.2, 2.8 and 12.0 slip events per period on its three bow cells against 2.1, 2.0 and 4.0) and ties its page at 11 of 14 (attack comes inside, cepstral envelope goes outside), but it now reads 41.8 dB harmonics-to-noise against 37.9 in the recording and holds a line at 301.3 Hz, -39.1 dB re its first harmonic, where the last page read -57.5 dB. The stopped notes' force is a rule chosen for these pages, the window's geometric mean; the open pages' forces sit higher (0.78 to 0.80 on a log scale); a measured player's bow force for a stopped cello note at a known bow distance would replace the rule

lines that are not harmonics: C2's line near 175 Hz reads 176.8 Hz, 9.8 dB over the recording over 0.5-1.4 s, and its 163.9 Hz line sits at the recording's level there; neither is traced; Eb4's cluster at 165-195 Hz is now -46 dB re its first harmonic (it was -36), the recording's level, but its strongest line is now 301.3 Hz at -39.1 dB re its first harmonic, 12.3 Hz under its note, at the frequency of a shell mode in the s8 table (300.27 Hz; this body's own table was not made) where the recording's strongest line between 285 and 309 Hz is 293.3 Hz at -53.5 dB; no grader row measures it
the other strings: only the bowed string is on a card, so there is no sympathetic ringing and no string-to-string coupling through the body
the rosin's temperature-dependent behaviour, transfer layer and contact history: eq. 13 is a velocity law measured at steady sliding
the endpin's floor contact and the player's hold on the ribs: the point mass on A3, D3 and C2 carries neither, and neither is modelled

torsion on the other strings and on stopped notes: only the open D3 string has a measured torsion row (Mansour, Woodhouse and Scavone 2016, Part 2); the row refuses a stop profile, so the stopped notes cannot take it, and no other string of the set is measured. D3's own torsion row did not close any of its holes: with the endpin and the printed bar, re the strongest harmonic over 1.0-1.9 s, H5, H7 and H9 sit 9.1, 8.5 and 12.3 dB under the recording and H3, H8 and H10 14.2, 11.3 and 35.4 dB over it, and its centroid is 358 Hz against 215
